title: DecisionScoreResult
description: ADVISORY output of the optional decision scorer (docs/architecture/decision-layer.md section 4). It ranks candidates the core already authorised and nothing more: it is raw scorer output that the core gates (confidence, calibration, candidate size, out-of-distribution), and every selected candidate ID is re-resolved by the deterministic application adapter before any use. It is never an authorisation, a permission, an approval, a validation, a preparation, a confirmation or a commit, no property is named or shaped like one, and no API, SDK or document may present it as one. Either disposition is accepted (the gates passed, so the core may use the ranking as one input to choosing an interpretation path) or fallback (a typed fallback_reason says why the ranking is not used and the controller path runs). Every property has authority alixai: the scorer raw output is advisory input, and the core stamps and checks each field after the call.

disposition.description: accepted: the confidence, calibration, size and out-of-distribution gates passed, so the ranking may inform which interpretation path the core takes; it authorises nothing. fallback: the ranking is not used; fallback_reason says why.

fallback_reason.description: Why the ranking is not used. Present exactly when disposition is fallback.

provider_id.description: The decision provider that produced, or was asked to produce, the result.

model_id.description: The scorer model that produced the ranking. Present when disposition is accepted; may be absent on a fallback that never reached a model (for example disabled or resource_gate).

model_revision.description: The pinned revision of the model, compared with the scorer manifest and the model registry (a difference is model_mismatch). Present when disposition is accepted.

contract_version.description: The conversation-contract version of the request this result answers.

decision_type.description: The kind of bounded choice that was ranked.

schema_version.description: The version of the decision-type contract this result follows.

tenant_id.description: The tenant of the request, echoed so the core can reject a result that belongs to another tenant (tenant_mismatch).

application_id.description: The application of the request, echoed for the same check.

selections.description: The candidates the scorer ranks highest, best first, at most 8. Empty exactly when disposition is fallback. Each ID must be one of the request candidate IDs; an ID that is not is malformed_output. Advisory: every ID is re-resolved by the deterministic adapter before use.

ood_status.description: Whether the input looked like what the scorer was calibrated on. in_distribution: it did. out_of_distribution: it did not. unsupported_shape: its shape is not one the scorer supports. not_evaluated: the scorer was never run. An accepted result is always in_distribution.

latency_ms.description: Wall-clock time spent obtaining the result, in milliseconds. 0 when the scorer was not called.

cache_status.description: hit: the ranking came from the decision cache. miss: it was computed. bypassed: the cache was not consulted.

trace_id.description: Trace ID of the scoring call, to correlate this result with the provider call.

audit_ref.description: Reference to the audit record of this scoring attempt.

issued_at.description: When the core recorded the result.

allOf.description: An accepted result names its model and revision, selects at least one candidate and was in distribution; it has no fallback reason.

selection.description: One candidate the scorer ranks highly, with its raw score and its calibrated confidence. Advisory: a high score never makes a candidate authorised.

candidate_id.description: The candidate, by the ID it had in the request. Re-resolved by the deterministic adapter before use.

score.description: The scorer raw score for the candidate, 0 to 1. Not comparable across models or revisions.

calibrated_confidence.description: The score after calibration, 0 to 1: the estimated probability that the scorer is right, as measured on the calibration set. Compared with the confidence gate; never a guarantee.
